## Standing preamble (portability across accounts on this machine)

This pack, and this whole project, live under one repository checkout on this machine. That checkout's own absolute path is masked above and everywhere else this generator writes it, on purpose: this repository is public, and every generated section of every pack page is routed through this project's own path-masking funnel before it reaches disk. Get the real path with `pwd` run from inside the checkout, or by reading PROJECT.md's own "Canonical path" line at the project root (recorded there in the same $HOME-relative form for the same reason). Whatever that path is, `cd` there before running anything below.

Run every tool as `python3 tools/<name>.py`, FROM the repository root, never by name alone. An installed copy of this project's tools can live under the Claude Code harness's own skills directory, and that installed copy can sit at an OLDER store schema than this repository's own store; invoked by name it refuses with a schema-ahead error instead of running. Running `python3 tools/<name>.py` from this checkout is never wrong; running whatever the shell happens to have on PATH can be.

This session's own write-scope label (the `bm1-<hash>` shape a record or STATE.md may show) is DERIVED, never chosen and never copied. tools/bm_fence_hook.py computes it from this session's own harness session id (BM_FENCE_SESSION_ID or CLAUDE_SESSION_ID) the first time it claims or checks a fence, and any earlier label printed in STATE.md or on a record belongs to WHICHEVER session claimed it, never to this one. A fresh session, on a fresh account, derives its own the first time it claims anything; it never reuses a label read off a page.

The project's store, STATE.md, and the .sbe/ evidence directory are all machine-local: none of the three is tracked in git (see .gitignore), so all three are inherited by whoever sits at this machine and this checkout, regardless of which Claude account is running the session. Nothing about switching accounts on this same machine requires rebuilding any of them.

The ONE thing that genuinely does not carry across accounts is the published progress artifact. Its URL belongs to the account that published it (PROJECT.md's own "Published artifact URL" line), and a different account cannot update that same URL. A session picking this work up under a different account delivers the board's own HTML file instead (the board copy in THIS pack, named in 00-READ-ME-FIRST.md, or a freshly generated one) and must NOT publish a second, competing artifact for this same project: one current board, one URL, owned by whichever account first published it.

## Standing lessons

- PO-1, the gate recipe, exactly: clear the sentinel file FIRST, detach the run, poll the process rather than a fixed sleep, and keep hands off the tree while it runs. The gate refuses a dirty tree.
- git add every new file, THEN regenerate the manifest (CHECKSUMS.sha256) LAST, then commit. Regenerating before a new file is added silently omits it from the manifest.
- The delivery scans (secret, dash, attribution, private-terms, and whichever others this project runs) are grep-shaped, and a grep that finds nothing exits 1, not 0. Read the exit code; a scan step that is not checked is not a scan.
- Claim write scope in BOTH registries before writing a single byte, under this session's own DERIVED label. A session never reuses a label a previous session printed; see the STANDING PREAMBLE above for how a label is derived.
- A worktree agent's tree starts at HEAD, not at the main tree's uncommitted state. Uncommitted work in the main checkout is invisible to it until that work is committed.
- Ask a control for its own answer rather than re-deriving that answer by hand (grep, manual parse, a second reader of the same file format). Two readers of one format drift silently. NO-DATA is never a pass, whichever way the answer was reached.
- Every dated document carries a status line in its first 25 lines.
- A complaint closes with code plus a regression test that fails on the pre-fix shape, never with prose alone.
- Nothing lands after a release-cut commit until the tag is pushed; the tag is a founder gate.
